title: feat(app-shell): read-only current-organization indicator for single-membership users
body:
Fixes #5287

A user with exactly one organization membership now sees the current
organization name in the console top bar, read-only, on deployments whose
tenancy posture puts an organization wall in force. Option A as ruled
(2026-08-19, 「全部接受」); the workspace switcher stays hidden when there is
nothing to switch to.

## The file surface (the card named it by behaviour)

The top bar is not in `apps/console` at all — the console app mounts
`@object-ui/app-shell`'s `AppHeader`. Everything is in `packages/app-shell`:

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/app-shell/src/layout/CurrentOrganizationIndicator.tsx` | new — the read-only indicator |
| `packages/app-shell/src/layout/OrgBadge.tsx` | new — the two-letter mark, extracted so both org surfaces share one |
| `packages/app-shell/src/layout/AppHeader.tsx` | mounts it beside the switcher (2 lines + a corrected comment) |
| `packages/app-shell/src/layout/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx` | uses the shared badge; **visibility rule untouched** |
| `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useTenancyPosture.ts` | adds `postureHasOrgWall` |
| `packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts` | one key, `organization.current.label`, in all ten packs |

## The precondition: outcome 1 — already present, no new fetch

Measured before the component was written, and the measurement is kept as a
pin (`packages/auth/src/__tests__/singleMembershipActiveOrg-5287.test.tsx`,
against the real `AuthProvider`, not a mock):

- `packages/auth/src/AuthProvider.tsx:646-652` — the effect that loads
  organizations gates on `user && enabled && !isPreviewMode` only. There is no
  membership-count condition, so a one-membership session fetches exactly like
  any other.
- `packages/auth/src/AuthProvider.tsx:567-611` — `refreshOrganizations` calls
  `client.listOrganizations()`, and lines 583-590 hold ADR-0081's
  single-membership repair: at `orgs.length === 1` it calls
  `setActiveOrganization(orgs[0].id)`, so `activeOrganization` is populated even
  for a session predating the server-side stamp.
- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/AppHeader.tsx:151-154` already destructures
  `activeOrganization` from `useAuth()`, and
  `packages/app-shell/src/layout/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx:76-77` computes
  `activeOrganization ?? orgList[0]` — then throws it away at the
  `orgList.length <= 1` early return.

**Cost: zero new requests, on any render.** The datum was in hand the whole
time; only the rendering was missing.

The zero was counter-probed before being believed: rendering `AppHeader` with a
one-membership `isolated` session found no organization name anywhere while the
user's own name rendered fine in the same tree. That counter-probe survives as
the first assertion pair in
`packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/AppHeader.singleMembershipOrg.test.tsx`.

## The other half: what a non-isolated deployment renders

Nothing new — and that is gated deliberately, not incidentally.

"Org context is active" is ADR-0105's tenancy posture, which the console already
reads in `useTenancyPosture`. The predicate is the protocol's own
`postureEnforcesWall` rule: true for `isolated` and `group`, false for `single`,
where the Layer 0 wall is inert and an organization is not a scope the user is
inside. An absent or unrecognized posture — older server, degraded deployment,
config fetch in flight or failed — renders nothing, matching every other
posture-keyed affordance in this repo.

### Why the rule is spelled locally instead of imported from the spec

Importing `postureEnforcesWall` from `@objectstack/spec/security` would be the
drift-proof spelling, but it is not free at this call site. Measured with the
repo's own esbuild, bundling the security subpath alongside a graph that
**already holds the entire spec root entry**:

```
root entry only            1271.8 KB   (minified)
root entry + /security     1509.1 KB   -> +237.3 KB
```

The security subpath's schema modules are a separate graph, and
`@objectstack/spec` declares no `sideEffects`, so nothing tree-shakes them away.
The consumer here is the top bar, i.e. the eager closure that this repo already
guards in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` (`assertLazyLinterStaysLazy`, added for
objectui#5266 over 89 KiB gzipped). A quarter megabyte on every page load to
spell a three-value predicate is the wrong trade.

The drift that import would have prevented is paid for at test time instead:
`packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/tenancyPostureWall.parity.test.ts`
imports the spec's real `postureEnforcesWall` and iterates `TENANCY_POSTURES`,
asserting the local predicate agrees for every posture the protocol declares.
Tests are not bundled, so that assertion costs nothing — and a posture added or
reclassified upstream fails CI here instead of silently rendering the wrong
chrome.

## Not option B

The rejected shape was a switcher rendering one disabled entry. This is a
separate component: `WorkspaceSwitcher`'s `orgList.length <= 1` early return is
unchanged, and the indicator renders a bare `span` — no trigger, no menu, no
click target, nothing focusable. A disabled control is still a control; this is
context, not navigation. Workspace management stays where objectstack#8096 put
it, in the avatar menu's "My Workspaces" entry.

## Tests

22 new assertions across four files, all four ruled cases covered:

- one membership + walled posture ⇒ name rendered, **no switcher control**;
- multiple memberships ⇒ unchanged, switcher renders, indicator stands down;
- `single` posture / no posture reported ⇒ nothing new renders anywhere;
- the indicator is genuinely read-only (no button, link, role, or tabindex).

Negative cases each wait for the async posture to actually arrive before
reading an absence — otherwise "nothing rendered" would pass on timing alone,
against a component with no gate at all.

### Reverse verification, predicted before running

No build artifact sits between the edit and any of these tests: every
`@object-ui/*` specifier is aliased to `src` in `vitest.config.mts:245-283`, and
the tests import the components by relative path. The one dist in the picture is
`@objectstack/spec` in the parity test, an unmodified published dependency.

**Leg 1 — ablate the render** (the indicator returns null, i.e. today's
behaviour). Predicted 5 red: 4 in the component file (both render cases,
read-only, assistive-tech), 1 in the header file, 0 in the parity file, 0 in the
auth measurement. **Observed: exactly that, 5 failed / 17 passed.** The auth
measurement staying green is the point — it measures the datum, not the render,
so it could never have caught this defect on its own.

**Leg 2 — ablate the gate** (`postureHasOrgWall` returns true always).
Predicted 8 red: 4 negative cases in the component file, 2 in the header file,
2 in the parity file. **Observed 9 failed / 13 passed — one more than
predicted.** The miss: `postureHasOrgWall(undefined)` also flips to true under
that ablation, so the parity file's "unresolved posture reads as no wall" case
went red too. Nothing about the change is different from what was predicted;
the prediction under-counted a case the same one-line predicate governs.

Both restores verified byte-clean (zero ablation markers left, `git status`
clean apart from the then-untracked changeset), and the suite re-run green.

### Run at `b2999569a`, the final commit

```
vitest packages/app-shell/src/layout packages/app-shell/src/hooks   54 files, 432 passed
vitest packages/i18n packages/auth                                  64 files, 1018 passed
vitest (the 4 files above)                                           4 files,  22 passed
pnpm --filter @object-ui/{app-shell,auth,i18n} type-check            Done
check:i18n-keys / check:i18n-drift / check:control-bytes             exit 0
check-changeset-presence / check-changeset-no-major                  exit 0
check:phantom-deps / check:self-import                               exit 0
eslint (9 changed files)                                             0 errors
```

`check:i18n-keys` confirms the new key resolves against the `en` pack and its
inline `defaultValue` matches the value the pack serves.

## Changeset

`minor` for `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n` (new user-visible
surface, new translated string). Never `major`. The `@object-ui/auth` change is
a test file only, so it declares nothing.
